title: A root names its languages in _root.md and the pack stops, stems and folds its questions by them, with a tiny German and Polish fixture root
goal: _root.md may carry languages: en, de (default en = today's behaviour, byte-identical packs for every existing root). Per-language data under _tools/lang/<code>/ (stop words, suffix rules, optional folding variants such as ö/oe and ł/l). Stop words are the union of the served roots' languages; each indexed unit is stemmed by its own root's profile and the query once per root it is matched against; a folding variant counts as present like an alias and is never a key word. A tiny German and a tiny Polish fixture root with held-out questions in those languages answer good where the fact is present and none where it is not; the public eval shares and the test ids stay unchanged.

run: import os,subprocess,sys; env=dict(os.environ,KB_ROOTS='_tools/fixtures/lang/de'); o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/rag.py','pack','--root','lang-de','--format','concise','Wie lade ich X im Kartenskript?'],env=env,capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout; assert 'coverage: good' in o, o[:400]

gates.question: What happens when a root's languages names a code that has no data under _tools/lang/?
options: Refuse the root with a RootError naming the code and the codes that exist
Serve it with the English profile and print a warning
gates.recommendation: Refuse the root with a RootError naming the code and the codes that exist
gates.reason: because a silent fallback hides a typo as a quietly wrong verdict
gates.answer: Refuse the root with a RootError naming the code and the codes that exist

gates.question: Which language data ships in the repository, and may a root bring its own?
options: de and pl only, in _tools/lang/, the two the fixtures prove; a root cannot bring its own yet
de and pl in _tools/lang/ and a root may add its own under its _retrieval/ directory
A wider set (es, fr, it, nl) in _tools/lang/
gates.recommendation: de and pl only, in _tools/lang/, the two the fixtures prove; a root cannot bring its own yet
gates.reason: because untested stop lists and suffix rules cost correct verdicts and a root-owned profile can be added later without changing the format
gates.answer: de and pl in _tools/lang/ and a root may add its own under its _retrieval/ directory

gates.question: Do the German and Polish held-out questions count in the public held-out answer rate (lookup_heldout.csv, 86 of 99)?
options: No: the fixture roots carry their own held-out file and eval, the public rate and its sprint-review bar stay as they are
Yes: add them to the public held-out file
gates.recommendation: No: the fixture roots carry their own held-out file and eval, the public rate and its sprint-review bar stay as they are
gates.reason: because the public file measures English facts about Windows management and mixing in fixture questions would blur that bar

notes: Premise (run at plan time): kbfacts.key_terms('How do I load X in a usermap?') -> ['load', 'usermap']; key_terms('Wie lade ich X im Kartenskript?') -> ['wie', 'lade', 'ich', 'im', 'kartenskript'] (wie, ich, im count as key words); key_terms('Kartenskripte laden Karten') -> ['kartenskript', 'laden', 'karten'] (no German suffix stripped: laden stays laden). Reproduces at the key-word level. The pack-level good-versus-none verdict was not re-run: it needs the fixture root this story adds (no German root exists to run it on). _meta() in kbcommon.py reads one flat key: value per line, so languages needs a list parse. The index unit cache key already hashes STOP, kbid.STOP and the token patterns (kf_index.py _weigh_data), so profile data must enter that hash and INDEX_VERSION bumps. Existing readers of kbfacts.STOP (bench_pool, factdiff, kbid, kbtools, ql_apply, ql_learn) keep the English base set and need no edit if the union is a new function. Overlap: ST-q5o7z2mf (sprint SP-jwvaq2hu) touches _tools/rag.py, AGENTS.md, kb/_self/tools.md; this story touches kb/_self/tools.md too, so land after it or rebase.
